# Cub Hub (Team Wolf for Kids)

> The Cub Hub is Team Wolf's free website for kids ages 8 to 12 (about grades 3 to 7). It teaches how Gray Wolves live with seven short lessons, wolf games, videos, printable coloring pages and fact cards, and a letter kids can send to their governor with a grown-up. Team Wolf is a coalition of wildlife advocates, outdoor people, educators and scientists working to keep Gray Wolves a permanent part of the American wild.

## Main pages

- [The Rendezvous](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/): Seven short wolf lessons for kids ages 8 to 12, with real wolf photos, tap-to-learn facts and a badge for every lesson. Free, from Team Wolf.
- [Videos](https://teamwolf.kids/videos/): Three short wolf videos made for kids: the history of wolves, the myth of the Big Bad Wolf, and living alongside wolves. Plus live wolf cams.
- [Games](https://teamwolf.kids/play/): Free wolf games for kids: wolf trivia, a wolf crossword, Howl-Along, Whose Tracks?, Trail Cam Detective, Raven Tag, a funny fill-in and a joke generator.
- [Coloring](https://teamwolf.kids/color/): Free printable wolf coloring pages for kids, including pages drawn by Team Wolf members. Pick a page, print it and color.
- [Write a Letter](https://teamwolf.kids/letter/): Kids can write a letter to their governor about wolves: fill in the boxes, print it, sign it, and send it with a grown-up.
- [Help Wolves](https://teamwolf.kids/help/): Ten easy ways kids can help wolves and wild animals, with a checklist to tick off.
- [For Grown-Ups](https://teamwolf.kids/parents/): What the Cub Hub is and how to use it with kids: wolf books by age, a teacher’s guide to the wolf lessons, and the team behind it.

## The Rendezvous: seven wolf lessons

Each lesson takes about 10 minutes and ends with a badge.

### [Lesson 1: Meet the Wolf](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-1/)

Gray Wolves are the biggest wild members of the dog family. Here’s what makes them amazing.

- Every dog on Earth, from Chihuahuas to Great Danes, comes from ancient wolves.
- A wolf’s sense of smell is about 100 times stronger than yours.
- A grown wolf is 3 to 5 feet long, not counting its tail.
- Gray Wolves aren’t only gray. They can be black, white, tan, or a mix.
- Wolf pups are born with blue eyes. They turn gold as the pups grow up.
- Two kinds of wolves live in the United States today: the Gray Wolf and the Red Wolf. Red Wolves are critically endangered.

### [Lesson 2: The Pack Is a Family](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-2/)

A wolf pack isn’t a gang. It’s a family that lives, travels, and raises pups together.

- A pack is usually 7 or 8 wolves: a mom, a dad, and their kids.
- Pups are born in the spring, about 5 at a time.
- Newborn pups can’t see or hear yet, and they weigh about 1 pound.
- Pups play tag, hide-and-seek, and wrestle. Playing teaches them how to hunt and get along.
- Young wolves stay with their family for at least 2 years. Then some leave to start packs of their own.

### [Lesson 3: Why Wolves Howl](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-3/)

A howl is how wolves talk across long distances. Every pack has its own howl.

- Wolves howl to find each other when the pack is spread out.
- A howl tells other packs, “This is our home. Stay away.”
- Packs often howl together before they head out to hunt.
- Wolves also whimper, bark, growl, and yelp, a lot like dogs do.
- Wolves don’t howl at the moon. But they do howl more when the moon is full and bright.

### [Lesson 4: What Wolves Eat](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-4/)

Wolves are carnivores, which means they eat meat. They’re a big part of the food web.

- In Yellowstone, wolves mostly eat elk. They also eat deer, moose, bison, and beavers.
- A hungry wolf can eat up to 20 pounds of meat in one meal.
- Wolves often catch animals that are old, sick, or weak, which helps keep the herds healthy.
- Ravens share wolves’ leftovers all winter, and the two even play together.
- Leftovers also feed eagles, bears, and lots of other animals.

### [Lesson 5: The Yellowstone Story](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-5/)

When wolves came home to Yellowstone, the whole park changed.

- By 1926, people had killed every wolf in Yellowstone.
- For about 70 years, there were no wolves. Elk hung around the rivers and ate the young trees.
- In 1995, wolves were brought from Canada and set free in Yellowstone.
- Wolves are a keystone species. That means a whole ecosystem leans on them, like a stone arch leans on its keystone. Take wolves out and things fall out of balance.
- When wolves came back, trees grew back, beavers and songbirds returned, and the rivers changed.
- Today about 100 wolves live in Yellowstone.

### [Lesson 6: Wolves and People](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-6/)

People have told stories about wolves for thousands of years. Some got wolves right. Some got them very wrong.

- In an old Roman story, a she-wolf took care of two baby brothers, Romulus and Remus. Romulus grew up to found the city of Rome.
- Other Plains tribes called the Pawnee “the Wolf People,” because Pawnee scouts moved as quietly as wolves.
- The Mohegan people take their name from a word meaning “wolf.” They first lived in what is now upstate New York, then settled in Connecticut.
- The Ojibwe people call the wolf Ma’iingan. They teach that what happens to wolves happens to people too.
- Stories like Little Red Riding Hood made wolves look like villains. Real wolves are shy and usually stay far away from people.

### [Lesson 7: Wolves Need Us](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/lesson-7/)

Wolves are still in trouble. The good news? Kids like you can help.

- About 8,000 Gray Wolves live in the lower 48 states today, in ten states.
- Wolves now live on only about 10% of the land they used to call home.
- In Alaska, Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming, wolves aren’t protected from hunting. People there are allowed to hunt them for sport.
- Wolves can’t write letters. You can. Every voice counts.

## Games

- [Wolf Trivia for Kids](https://teamwolf.kids/play/quiz/): Wolf trivia for kids at three levels, from Beginner to Wolf Expert. Every answer comes with a real wolf fact.
- [Wolf Crossword for Kids](https://teamwolf.kids/play/crossword/): A wolf crossword puzzle for kids, with hints. Every answer is a wolf fact you can find on the Cub Hub. Play online or print it.
- [What's Your Wolf Pack Role?](https://teamwolf.kids/play/packgame/): Type your first name to find out which job you'd have in a wolf pack, and learn how a wolf family works together.
- [Howl-Along: Make a Wolf Chorus](https://teamwolf.kids/play/howlAlong/): Tap wolves to hear real wolf howls and build a whole pack chorus.
- [Bring the Wolves Back to Yellowstone](https://teamwolf.kids/play/buildpack/): A kids game: add wolves, willows, beavers, songbirds and ravens in the right order to bring a Yellowstone valley back to life.
- [Wolf Funny Fill-in](https://teamwolf.kids/play/fillin/): Fill in the blanks to make a silly wolf story. A word game for kids.
- [Whose Tracks? Animal Track Matching Game](https://teamwolf.kids/play/tracks/): Match real animal track photos to the animals that made them, the way wildlife scientists do.
- [Trail Cam Detective](https://teamwolf.kids/play/trailcam/): Watch real trail-camera videos and guess which animal got caught on camera.
- [Raven Tag](https://teamwolf.kids/play/ravtag/): Play the pup: jump for the stick the way wolf pups play with ravens in Yellowstone.
- [Wolf Joke Generator](https://teamwolf.kids/play/jokes/): Wolf jokes for kids to tell their pack.

## More to explore

- [Track the Pack](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/trackpack/): Slide through time to see where wolves lived long ago, when they almost disappeared, and where they live today.
- [Wolf-Birds](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/wolfbirds/): A true picture story for kids about how ravens and wolves live, eat and play together in Yellowstone.
- [Fact Pack](https://teamwolf.kids/learn/factpack/): 21 wolf fact cards kids can flip, share, or print to cut out and trade.
- [Wolf Books by Age](https://teamwolf.kids/parents/books/): A reading list of wolf books for kids and families, each with an age level.
- [Teacher’s Guide](https://teamwolf.kids/parents/teach/): A teacher’s guide to the Rendezvous: seven 10-minute wolf lessons for ages 8 to 12 that work on a classroom projector or one device per kid.
- [The Pack Behind the Cub Hub](https://teamwolf.kids/parents/team/): Team Wolf is a coalition of wildlife advocates, outdoor people, educators and scientists working to keep Gray Wolves a permanent part of the American wild. The Cub Hub is its program for kids.

## For grown-ups

Team Wolf's main site, for adults, is https://teamwolf.org.
